text:
Sunday (22 February) saw the clash of the ages, as the USA and Canada battled for the title of 2026 Olympic champion, with Jack Hughes securing the gold in 2-1 overtime victory.
Forty-six years to the day after the "Miracle on Ice*"* team played their way into ice hockey lore at Lake Placid 1980, the United States created a new Olympic memory for fans to dream about, defeating Canada 2-1 in overtime in the men’s final at Olympic Winter Games Milano Cortina 2026 on Sunday (22 February). 
It marks the third Olympic gold medal for the United States in men’s ice hockey, and the first since their win in Upstate New York.
Jack Hughes was the hero, scoring the golden goal in overtime to secure gold for the Americans. Smiling afterward, a gap visible where a tooth once stood, Hughes modestly downplayed his personal moment.
“It doesn’t matter about the goal. Just an unbelievable team, unbelievable team win. We’re so proud to be American and to win for our country, to win for the USA Hockey brotherhood,” said the star forward who plays for the National Hockey League’s New Jersey Devils.
“Listen – they probably outplayed us a little bit tonight. Our goalie stood on his head, though, and in overtime, we both have skilled players, so anything can happen.”
U.S. goaltender Connor Hellebuyck (Winnipeg Jets) was the backbone of that victory, stopping 41 shots to keep the Americans’ dreams alive. Without him, the outcome almost certainly would have been different.
“Unbelievable game by Hellebuyck,” Hughes added. “He was our best player tonight by a mile. That’s just a gutsy win. That’s American hockey right there.”
What a tournament it was for the Hughes family. Quinn Hughes (Minnesota Wild) scored the overtime winner against Sweden in the quarter-final, and his brother Jack followed with an overtime winner in the final. Their mother, Ellen, who works with the USA Hockey women’s team, also celebrated gold as the American women captured the Olympic title.
“He just loves the game more than anyone," Quinn said of his brother, still on the ice. "In this tournament, he showed he’s clearly one of the best players in the world.” 
With both the United States and Canada icing fully NHL-based rosters, the men’s Olympic ice hockey final truly delivered the highest level of international play possible.
Finland secured bronze one day earlier, defeating Slovakia 6-1 on Saturday (21 February). Earlier in the week, the United States beat Canada in the women’s final (also a 2-1 overtime decision), with several members of those teams present to support the men from the stands in a lively Milano Santagiulia Ice Hockey Arena.
